title: From deliberation to acclamation: how did Twitter's algorithms foster polarized communities and undermine democracy in the 2020 US presidential election

live_model.evidence: "we tested the prompts using GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, and GPT-3.5-turbo augmented with the COLA strategy"; "Simple accuracy is selected as the primary evaluation metric"

prompt.note: "five distinct prompts are designed" for stance classification, but none is quoted; only the label scheme (support/against/neutral) and per-user aggregation formulas are given.

claim.metric: none (accuracy values for GPT-4-turbo / prompt combinations are never reported)
claim.location: n/a; test set = 87 manually annotated tweets

data.source: 150,569 original tweets / 727,085 retweets collected via the Twitter API (2020 election); the 87-tweet annotated test set is not stated as released

notes: The paper states which models/prompts were compared and the metric used but never reports which combination won or its score; downstream analysis (Tables 1-3) covers only network centrality, not model performance.
